2027-03-14.title: Samio Sunday · The Healing of the Blind
readings: Solomon asks for an understanding mind
The Lord made the earth by his power
2027-03-14.alt: Sixth Sunday of the Great Fast. The Fortieth Day of the Fast is Friday 19 March; Lazarus Saturday is 20 March; Hosanna Sunday is 21 March: remind the faithful to bring palm leaves and flowers.
2027-03-14.verse: One thing I do know, that though I was blind, now I see.
theo: On the last Sunday before Holy Week the Church reads two healings of the blind. In John, Jesus meets a man blind from birth. The disciples ask whose sin caused it. Jesus answers: “Neither this man nor his parents sinned; he was born blind so that God's works might be revealed in him… As long as I am in the world, I am the light of the world.” He makes mud, anoints the man's eyes, and sends him: “Go, wash in the pool of Siloam (which means Sent).”

The healed man is questioned again and again by the Pharisees. He does not know all the theology, but he knows one thing: “Though I was blind, now I see.” Step by step his sight grows: first “the man called Jesus”, then “a prophet”, then, kneeling before him, “Lord, I believe.” Meanwhile those who claim to see become blind. Jesus says: “I came into this world for judgment so that those who do not see may see, and those who do see may become blind.”

In Mark, blind Bartimaeus sits by the road at Jericho and cries out: “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!” People tell him to be quiet; he cries out louder. Jesus asks: “What do you want me to do for you?” “My teacher, let me see again.” “Go; your faith has made you well.” And Bartimaeus “followed him on the way”, the way to Jerusalem and the Cross.

Job, after all his suffering, says: “I had heard of you by the hearing of the ear, but now my eye sees you.” This is the goal of the Fast: not only to hear about God, but to see him with the eyes of faith. In Baptism, called “enlightenment” by the Fathers, we were washed and given sight. As Holy Week begins, let us ask with Bartimaeus: “Lord, let me see,” and then follow Jesus on the way.
conn: The man washes in the pool called Sent, and Jesus is the One sent by the Father: the Fathers saw here an image of Baptism, the washing that gives sight.
Jesus makes clay as God formed Adam from the earth (Genesis 2:7): a new creation.
Solomon asked for an understanding mind (1 Kings 3:9); true sight is wisdom from God.
Bartimaeus follows Jesus “on the way” to Jerusalem (Mark 10:52): healed disciples walk with him to the Cross.
altar: The Fathers called Baptism “illumination” and the Eucharist the food of those who see. At the Holy Qurbono we pray with Bartimaeus: “Have mercy on us”, and we receive the Light of the world.
outline: What is the worst kind of blindness?
Jesus opens eyes: new creation, Siloam, Baptism.
From “a man called Jesus” to “Lord, I believe”.
Point 3 · Those who think they see
Bartimaeus: cry out, receive sight, follow to Jerusalem.
live: Repeat during the day: “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me.”
Bring palm leaves and flowers on Sunday; plan to attend the services of Holy Week.
Examine honesty in business, weights, wages and taxes.
fathers: The man born blind is the human race; the clay is the Word made flesh; the washing in Siloam is Baptism, by which we are enlightened (Tractates on John 44).
With the clay he formed eyes as he had formed Adam from the dust; the Creator showed himself in the creating hand (Commentary on the Diatessaron).
magis: Baptism is called “enlightenment”, because those who receive it are enlightened in their understanding.
Jesus hears the prayer of faith: “Son of David, have mercy on me”; the Jesus Prayer comes from such cries.
Faith is a light that illumines every aspect of human existence.
saints: 17 Mar: St Patrick. 18 Mar: St Cyril of Jerusalem. 19 Mar: St Joseph, and in 2027 also the Fortieth Day of the Great Fast. 20 Mar: Lazarus Saturday.
2027-03-14.prayer: Lord Jesus, light of the world, you opened the eyes of the man born blind and of Bartimaeus. Have mercy on us: heal our blindness, let us see you with the eyes of faith, and give us grace to follow you on the way to Jerusalem, to your Cross and your Resurrection. Amen.

quick: Jesus is the light of the world: he opens blind eyes.
Faith grows step by step: “Lord, I believe.”
Bartimaeus receives sight and follows Jesus on the way.
2027-03-14.action: Pray often this week: “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me.”
2027-03-14.question: Where am I still blind, and do I want to see?
2027-03-14.special: Samio Sunday, sixth Sunday of the Great Fast. Announce the Fortieth Friday (19 Mar), Lazarus Saturday (20 Mar) and Hosanna Sunday (21 Mar); remind the faithful to bring palm leaves and flowers.
illus: Free eye camps in Kerala villages give sight to hundreds every year. One old man, after his cataract operation, said: “Now I can see my grandchildren's faces.” Jesus came to give us a sight even greater: to see God's face in Christ.

family.explain: A blind man called Bartimaeus shouted to Jesus for help. Jesus asked what he wanted, and he said: “I want to see!” Jesus healed him, and he followed Jesus.
family.intention: We pray for the blind and for those who have lost faith.
family.ask: Ask: “How will our family keep Holy Week this year?”

kidsaint: The husband of Mary and the foster father of Jesus, a carpenter who worked hard, protected his family and obeyed God at once. Lesson: work well and take care of your family.
term: Samio is Syriac for “the blind man”. The sixth Sunday of the Great Fast, the last before Hosanna Sunday, reads the healing of the blind.
termMore: The Fortieth Friday and Lazarus Saturday

On the Friday before Hosanna Sunday the forty days of the Fast are completed (the lectionary notes no fasting or prostrations that day). The next day remembers the raising of Lazarus, and Holy Week follows.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, on the last Sunday before Holy Week we hear of two blind men who receive their sight. In John's Gospel a man blind from birth; in Mark's, Bartimaeus, a beggar sitting by the road at Jericho.

Jesus makes clay, anoints the blind man's eyes and sends him to wash in the pool of Siloam, which means “Sent”. He comes back seeing. Then come the questions, the arguments, the threats. He does not know how to answer the scholars, but he knows one thing: “I was blind; now I see.” And his faith grows until he kneels and says: “Lord, I believe.” Meanwhile those who are sure they see refuse the light.

Bartimaeus cannot see, but he can shout. “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!” People tell him to be quiet. He shouts louder. Jesus stops and asks: “What do you want me to do for you?” “Teacher, let me see again.” He receives his sight and follows Jesus on the road, the road to Jerusalem.

Next Sunday is Hosanna. Holy Week begins. Let us ask Jesus to heal our blindness: to the poor beside us, to our own sins, to God's love. Let us pray Bartimaeus' prayer all through this week. And having received our sight, let us follow Jesus on the way, to his Cross and his Resurrection. Amen.
kids: Children, close your eyes for a moment. Now open them! It's wonderful to see, isn't it? Bartimaeus was blind. He heard Jesus was passing and shouted: “Jesus, help me!”
People said, “Be quiet!” But he shouted even louder. Jesus asked: “What do you want?” “I want to see!” And Jesus gave him his sight!
Next week we will wave palms for Jesus. Let's say: “Jesus, open my eyes to see you!”

intro: Theme: “I was blind, now I see.”

The Gospel of the man born blind is a journey from darkness to light, from not seeing to believing and worshipping. It is also our story: Baptism is called “illumination”, and Lent prepares us to see Christ more clearly.

sub: The disciples ask: who sinned, this man or his parents?
Jesus refuses that easy answer: God's works will be revealed in him.
Isaiah promised a day when the eyes of the blind would be opened: Christ brings that day.
q: Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf unstopped.
Jesus answered, “Neither this man nor his parents sinned; he was born blind so that God's works might be revealed in him.”
points.apply: Never judge the suffering of others as God's punishment; offer help instead.

points.h: Go and wash: the light of Baptism
sub: Jesus makes mud, anoints the man's eyes, and sends him to the pool of Siloam, “Sent”.
He obeys, washes and comes back seeing: an image of Baptism, the sacrament of enlightenment.
Solomon prayed for an understanding mind; true sight is to see as God sees.
q: Give your servant therefore an understanding mind to govern your people, able to discern between good and evil.
“Go, wash in the pool of Siloam” (which means Sent). Then he went and washed and came back able to see.
points.apply: Renew your baptismal faith: pray the Creed slowly each day this week.

points.h: From sight to faith and worship
sub: Questioned and expelled, the man holds to what he knows: “I was blind, now I see.”
Meeting Jesus again, he believes and worships: “Lord, I believe.”
Like Job, he moves from hearing about God to seeing him; like Bartimaeus, he follows Jesus on the way.
q: I had heard of you by the hearing of the ear, but now my eye sees you.
One thing I do know, that though I was blind, now I see. … He said, “Lord, I believe.” And he worshiped him.
points.apply: Share your simple testimony with someone: what Christ has done for you.

concl: Christ is the light of the world. The real blindness is to refuse to see him.
Let us wash, believe and worship, and walk as children of light toward Easter.
2027-03-14.resolve: Spend fifteen minutes before the Blessed Sacrament this week, asking: “Lord, let me see.”
